title: The Commish Hands Philly a Running Back and the Model Hands Philly the Keys
dek: Sonny sends Chuba Hubbard and DeVonta Smith to Alan for George Pickens and Ollie Gordon II, and the title odds swing 17 points in Team Pillbert's direction.
body: Before Week 6, two of the league's three 4-1 teams decided to do business. Sonny's The Horse is Hea sent running back Chuba Hubbard and wide receiver DeVonta Smith to Alan's Team Pillbert for wide receiver George Pickens and running back Ollie Gordon II. On raw production, Philly came out ahead: Hubbard (74) and Smith (39) had combined for 113 points before the deal, while Pickens (55) and Gordon (31.8) totaled 86.8. That's a 26.2-point gap, handed from one first-place team to another.

Start with the commish's side, where the case is better than the totals suggest. Gordon has scored 31.8 in just two weeks on a roster, a 15.9-a-week pace that is the best rate of any player in this deal. Pickens has averaged 11 a week over five weeks, which beats Smith's 7.8. Hubbard is the piece Sonny had trouble using: he arrived in the Rashee Rice deal and never cracked The Horse is Hea's lineup, including a 25.4-point week spent on the bench. Turning a guy you won't start into two guys you might is a defensible idea.

Alan's side is simpler. Hubbard is the headliner, 74 points in five weeks, about 14.8 a week, and he joins a backfield that already has Jahmyr Gibbs coming off a 35.2-point game. Smith adds a fourth receiver room option to a team that has been collecting them all month. There's also a small boomerang here: Gordon was one of Philly's own waiver pickups, so Alan essentially flipped a recent add into Hubbard. Phillibert's trading this season has been loud, and the model has punished it more than once. Not this time.

The verdict is lopsided. Team Pillbert's title odds jumped from 16% to 26%, a 10-point leap, while The Horse is Hea fell from 18% to 11%, a 7-point drop. A week ago Sonny had just passed Alan in the odds; now he's 15 points behind him. In fairness to the commish, he controls the league website, not the projection model, and the model has spoken. On paper, Alan wins this one clearly.

The schedule won't give either side a quiet debut. Sonny takes his new pair into the biggest game of Week 6 against Ramon's No Banner only HULK, the 55% favorite, where Gordon's rate and Pickens' consistency will need to look like an upgrade immediately. Alan gets Randy's The fumblers, and Hubbard gets to show the commish what a starting lineup slot looks like. Two 4-1 teams made this deal, and by Sunday night we'll know if both still deserve the number.

social.author: Pillbert Nation
social.text: 16% to 26%. Hubbard 74 points. Smith 39. The commissioner himself signed off on it. We would like to thank the league office for its cooperation.

social.author: Hea Hive
social.text: Ollie Gordon II: 15.9 a week. Best rate in the deal. Hubbard never started for us anyway. The model can keep its 7 points, we're keeping the vibes. Kickoff vs HULK, let's go.

social.author: Spreadsheet Steve
social.text: Received: 113 vs 86.8. Odds swing: +10 Pillbert, -7 Hea. Only bright spot for Sonny: Gordon outpaces everyone per week. Paper verdict: Philly, comfortably.

social.author: Fumblers Faithful
social.text: Cool, so the week we play Pillbert, they add a 74-point running back. Great timing, everybody. Really appreciate it.
